chunks.text: High vibration or vibration trip (Pumps, motors, vibrator motors): shaking, wobbling, jumping on the base, vibrating a lot, vib alarm, vibration trip, rough running
chunks.title: High vibration or vibration trip

chunks.text: Symptom SY-01: High vibration or vibration trip. Typical causes: Bearing wear; misalignment; loose base; impeller wear or imbalance; clogging. First check: Vibration pen reading and trend. First procedure: EM-01. Escalate if: ≥ 7.1 mm/s or rising fast; standby not available. Diagnostic questions: Is the reading 7.1 mm/s or more, or did the unit trip? Has vibration risen more than 1 mm/s in the last 7 days? Are base bolts or coupling loose or worn? Is the bearing temperature 80 °C or more?
chunks.title: High vibration or vibration trip

chunks.text: Unusual noise (grinding, rubbing, knocking) (Pumps, motors, screens): grinding, rubbing, knocking, squealing, screeching, rattling, metallic noise, noisy, loud
chunks.title: Unusual noise (grinding, rubbing, knocking)

chunks.text: Symptom SY-02: Unusual noise (grinding, rubbing, knocking). Typical causes: Bearing failure; coupling wear; impeller rubbing; loose parts. First check: Listen; vibration; temperature. First procedure: EM-01. Escalate if: Metal-to-metal rubbing. Diagnostic questions: Is the noise from the coupling area?
chunks.title: Unusual noise (grinding, rubbing, knocking)

chunks.text: Mechanical seal leak (Transfer pumps): leaking, dripping, drips, puddle under the pump, water on the floor, shaft leak, seal reservoir / oil cup level dropping
chunks.title: Mechanical seal leak

chunks.text: Symptom SY-03: Mechanical seal leak. Typical causes: Worn seal faces; abrasive fibre; dry running. First check: Leak rate; seal reservoir level. First procedure: EM-02. Escalate if: Leak > 20 drops/min or spraying. Diagnostic questions: Is the leak more than 5 drops per minute? Is the seal reservoir level falling? Is a spare seal set in stock?
chunks.title: Mechanical seal leak

chunks.text: Seal alarm / water in oil chamber (Submersible pumps): seal fault light, seal alarm, moisture sensor, water in oil, milky oil, submersible seal
chunks.title: Seal alarm / water in oil chamber

chunks.text: Symptom SY-04: Seal alarm / water in oil chamber. Typical causes: Lower seal failure. First check: Oil sample colour. First procedure: PR-17. Escalate if: Insulation ≤ 10 MΩ. Diagnostic questions: Is the oil milky or does it contain water drops?
chunks.title: Seal alarm / water in oil chamber

chunks.text: Low flow / flow drop (Pumps): weak flow, no water, not pumping, low discharge pressure, level not going down, sump not dropping, low m3/h, cubic
chunks.title: Low flow / flow drop

chunks.text: Symptom SY-05: Low flow / flow drop. Typical causes: Clogging; impeller wear; air lock; wrong rotation; check valve. First check: Flow vs baseline; current. First procedure: EM-03. Escalate if: Flow < 50% and level rising. Diagnostic questions: Is the pump current higher than normal? Are rags or fibre found at the impeller or strainer? Does the shaft turn backwards after stopping?
chunks.title: Low flow / flow drop

chunks.text: Pump will not start (Pumps): won't start, will not run, does not start, hums but no rotation, locked, seized, stuck, standby failed to start
chunks.title: Pump will not start

chunks.text: Symptom SY-06: Pump will not start. Typical causes: Seized shaft; tripped overload; no power; control fault. First check: Panel status; shaft turns by hand?. First procedure: EM-06. Escalate if: It is the standby and the duty has failed. Diagnostic questions: Is the overload or breaker tripped? Does the shaft turn freely by hand (after isolation)? Is there power at the panel and control circuit? Is this the standby and the duty unit has failed?
chunks.title: Pump will not start

chunks.text: Motor overload trip (Motors, submersibles, vibrator motors): overload, OL light, thermal relay tripped, breaker tripped, keeps tripping, trips on start, high current
chunks.title: Motor overload trip

chunks.text: Symptom SY-07: Motor overload trip. Typical causes: Clogging; low voltage; single phasing; bearing seizure. First check: Phase currents; shaft free?. First procedure: EM-05. Escalate if: Trips again after one reset. Diagnostic questions: Does it trip again within 5 minutes after one reset? Are the three phase currents balanced within 10%?
chunks.title: Motor overload trip

chunks.text: Motor or bearing overheating (Motors, pumps): hot, overheating, temperature high, smells hot, bearing hot, too hot to touch
chunks.title: Motor or bearing overheating

chunks.text: Symptom SY-08: Motor or bearing overheating. Typical causes: Blocked cooling; overload; bearing failure; lubrication. First check: IR temperature; current. First procedure: EM-07. Escalate if: Bearing ≥ 90 °C. Diagnostic questions: Is the fan cover blocked with fibre or fat? Is the motor current above 105% of full-load current?
chunks.title: Motor or bearing overheating

chunks.text: Burning smell, smoke or sparks (Motors, panels): burning smell, smoke, sparks, flash, arcing, fire at motor or panel
chunks.title: Burning smell, smoke or sparks

chunks.text: Symptom SY-09: Burning smell, smoke or sparks. Typical causes: Winding failure; loose termination; cable damage. First check: None – isolate first. First procedure: EM-08. Escalate if: Always escalate. Diagnostic questions: Is there smoke or visible sparks?
chunks.title: Burning smell, smoke or sparks

chunks.text: Earth-fault trip (Submersibles, motors): earth fault, ground fault, earth leakage, ELCB / RCD tripped, insulation low, cable cut or damaged
chunks.title: Earth-fault trip

chunks.text: Symptom SY-10: Earth-fault trip. Typical causes: Cable damage; moisture in motor. First check: Megger after isolation. First procedure: PR-18. Escalate if: Always escalate. Diagnostic questions: Is the cable sheath damaged?
chunks.title: Earth-fault trip

chunks.text: Crackling noise and fluctuating pressure (cavitation) (Transfer pumps): cavitation, crackling, gravel or stones sound, pressure fluctuating, low suction, EQ level low
chunks.title: Crackling noise and fluctuating pressure (cavitation)

chunks.text: Symptom SY-11: Crackling noise and fluctuating pressure (cavitation). Typical causes: Low EQ level; blocked strainer. First check: EQ level; strainer. First procedure: EM-04. Escalate if: Lasts > 1 h. Diagnostic questions: Is the EQ tank level below 30%?
chunks.title: Crackling noise and fluctuating pressure (cavitation)

chunks.text: Backflow / pump turns backwards after stop (Pumps): backflow, reverse rotation, turns backwards, check valve banging or slamming, water flowing back
chunks.title: Backflow / pump turns backwards after stop

chunks.text: Symptom SY-12: Backflow / pump turns backwards after stop. Typical causes: Check valve failure. First check: Check valve. First procedure: SV-02. Escalate if: Sump level rising with pump off. Diagnostic questions: Is the sump level rising while the pump is off?
chunks.title: Backflow / pump turns backwards after stop

chunks.text: Screen mesh blinded (cream/oil) (Screens): screen blinded, mesh full of fat or cream or oil, water going over the screen, overflowing screen
chunks.title: Screen mesh blinded (cream/oil)

chunks.text: Symptom SY-13: Screen mesh blinded (cream/oil). Typical causes: Fat and coconut cream build-up. First check: Mesh condition. First procedure: SV-07. Escalate if: Both screens blinded. Diagnostic questions: Is the other screen running and clean?
chunks.title: Screen mesh blinded (cream/oil)

chunks.text: Hole or tear in screen mesh (Screens): mesh torn, hole in mesh, mesh broken, solids passing to EQ tank
chunks.title: Hole or tear in screen mesh

chunks.text: Symptom SY-14: Hole or tear in screen mesh. Typical causes: Mesh fatigue; over-tension. First check: Visual; fibre downstream. First procedure: SV-01. Escalate if: Other screen not available. Diagnostic questions: Is the hole larger than the mesh opening (solids passing)? Is the other screen available?
chunks.title: Hole or tear in screen mesh

chunks.text: Sump or EQ tank level high (Sump, EQ tank): high level, sump overflowing, EQ tank full, level alarm high
chunks.title: Sump or EQ tank level high

chunks.text: Symptom SY-15: Sump or EQ tank level high. Typical causes: Pump pair down; inflow surge; level transmitter error. First check: Compare level with sight gauge. First procedure: EM-10. Escalate if: Level ≥ high-high. Diagnostic questions: Does the transmitter agree with the sight gauge within 5%? Are both pumps of the pair available?
chunks.title: Sump or EQ tank level high

chunks.text: Both pumps of a pair unavailable (Transfer or sump pair): both pumps down, no pump running, pair unavailable, duty tripped and standby won't start
chunks.title: Both pumps of a pair unavailable

chunks.text: Symptom SY-16: Both pumps of a pair unavailable. Typical causes: Duty failed and standby failed/under repair. First check: Buffer time on tablet. First procedure: EM-09. Escalate if: Always escalate. Diagnostic questions: Will the buffer run out within 1 hour?
chunks.title: Both pumps of a pair unavailable

chunks.text: Procedure OP-01 – Transfer pump start-up (Operation). Equipment: P-101A/B. Purpose: Start an EQ transfer pump safely and confirm normal running. When used: Daily changeover, after repair, after shutdown. Prerequisites: Seal reservoir level OK; suction valve open; EQ level above low-low. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses. Tools: Tablet, clamp meter. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: OP-01 Transfer pump start-up

chunks.text: OP-01 Transfer pump start-up – Step 1 (Preparation): Check the seal lubricant reservoir level and the casing for leaks. Accept: Reservoir level in normal band; no leaks. Step 2 (Preparation): Open suction valve fully; set discharge valve about one quarter open. Accept: Valve positions confirmed. Safety: Never start against a closed suction valve. Step 3 (Preparation): Confirm pump casing is full of liquid (vent until liquid appears). Accept: Steady liquid at vent. Safety: Splash hazard – face shield. Step 4 (Testing): Start the motor; within 10 s open the discharge valve slowly to full. Accept: Discharge pressure rises to ≈ 2.1 bar. Safety: Stop at once if no pressure in 30 s (dry running). Step 5 (Testing): Check rotation, noise and seal; take current with clamp meter. Accept: Current ≈ 11.5 A (≤ 12.8 A FLA); no abnormal noise. Step 6 (Close-out): Record start time and readings in the round on the tablet. Accept: Readings saved.
chunks.title: OP-01 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure OP-02 – Transfer pump shutdown (Operation). Equipment: P-101A/B. Purpose: Stop a transfer pump without water hammer or seal damage. When used: Daily changeover, before maintenance. Prerequisites: Partner pump started first (if changeover). PPE: Safety shoes, gloves. Tools: Tablet. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: OP-02 Transfer pump shutdown

chunks.text: OP-02 Transfer pump shutdown – Step 1 (Preparation): If this is a changeover, start the partner pump first (OP-01) and confirm flow. Accept: Partner running and stable. Step 2 (Isolation): Close the discharge valve slowly. Accept: Valve closed. Safety: Fast closing causes water hammer. Step 3 (Isolation): Stop the motor; confirm the shaft stops without reverse rotation. Accept: Shaft stopped; check valve holding. Safety: If shaft runs backwards, check valve has failed – raise work order. Step 4 (Isolation): Leave suction valve open (standby) or close it (maintenance). Accept: Valve set for next state. Step 5 (Close-out): Record stop time and reason. Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: OP-02 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure OP-03 – Daily duty/standby changeover (Operation). Equipment: PR-TRANSFER, PR-SUMP, PR-SCREEN. Purpose: Alternate duty and standby units every day so both stay ready. When used: Every day at day-shift start. Prerequisites: Both units available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves. Tools: Tablet. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: OP-03 Daily duty/standby changeover

chunks.text: OP-03 Daily duty/standby changeover – Step 1 (Preparation): Open today's rotation on the tablet; confirm which unit becomes duty. Accept: Rotation record shown. Step 2 (Testing): Start the standby unit (OP-01 for transfer pumps; local start for sump pump or screen). Accept: Starts normally; readings normal. Safety: If it fails to start: stop and use EM-06. Step 3 (Testing): Stop the former duty unit (OP-02) and leave it in standby. Accept: Former duty unit idle, valves set for standby. Step 4 (Close-out): Confirm changeover on the tablet; the system clears the missed-rotation alert. Accept: Rotation logged with time and initials. Safety: Never skip – a standby left idle for weeks may not start.
chunks.title: OP-03 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure OP-04 – Bring stored spare into service (Operation). Equipment: SP-P01, SP-P02, SP-M01, SP-VM01. Purpose: Install a stored spare in place of a failed or removed unit. When used: Failed unit removed for repair. Prerequisites: Spare readiness status Ready; latest check within 35 days. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, hard hat, safety glasses. Tools: Hoist/chain block, alignment kit, megger, torque wrench. Permits: Work permit; lifting plan. Parts: Coupling insert, gaskets.
chunks.title: OP-04 Bring stored spare into service

chunks.text: OP-04 Bring stored spare into service – Step 1 (Preparation): Check Spare_Readiness: status Ready, last IR test and preservation record. Accept: Status Ready; IR ≥ 100 MΩ (motors). Safety: Do not install a Not ready spare. Step 2 (Preparation): Remove preservation (covers, desiccant); turn shaft by hand. Accept: Shaft turns freely. Step 3 (Repair): Install the spare (PR-02/PR-03 for transfer pump; PR-16 for submersible). Accept: Installed per procedure. Safety: Lifting: never stand under load. Step 4 (Testing): Megger the motor before first start. Accept: ≥ 100 MΩ at 500 V DC (assumed acceptance). Step 5 (Testing): Run test (OP-05). Accept: Readings normal. Step 6 (Close-out): Update Equipment_Register location and Spare_Readiness (spare now in service); order repair of removed unit. Accept: Records updated.
chunks.title: OP-04 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure OP-05 – Return-to-service test run (Operation). Equipment: All pumps, motors, screens. Purpose: Prove a unit is fit after repair or long idle. When used: After any repair; after standby idle > 7 days. Prerequisites: Repair work order complete; guards fitted. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses. Tools: Vibration pen, IR thermometer, clamp meter. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: OP-05 Return-to-service test run

chunks.text: OP-05 Return-to-service test run – Step 1 (Testing): Start unit; listen for rubbing or knocking for the first minute. Accept: No abnormal noise. Safety: Stop at once on abnormal noise. Step 2 (Testing): After 15 min take vibration on DE and NDE bearings (horizontal and vertical). Accept: ≤ 2.8 mm/s good; 4.5 mm/s = alarm. Step 3 (Testing): After 30 min take bearing temperatures and motor current. Accept: Bearings ≤ 80 °C; current ≤ 105% FLA. Step 4 (Testing): Check seal (transfer pumps) or flow/current (submersibles). Accept: No visible leak; flow within 10% of rated. Step 5 (Close-out): Record readings as the new baseline for the unit. Accept: Baseline saved.
chunks.title: OP-05 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure OP-06 – Transfer pump priming and venting (Operation). Equipment: P-101A/B. Purpose: Remove air from the pump casing so it can pump. When used: After draining, after maintenance, after air-lock. Prerequisites: EQ tank level above pump centreline. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, face shield. Tools: Spanner. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: OP-06 Transfer pump priming and venting

chunks.text: OP-06 Transfer pump priming and venting – Step 1 (Preparation): Confirm EQ tank level is above pump centreline (flooded suction). Accept: Level ≥ 30%. Step 2 (Repair): Open suction valve; open casing vent slowly. Accept: Air then liquid at vent. Safety: Liquid may spray – face shield. Step 3 (Repair): Close vent when a steady liquid stream appears. Accept: No air in stream. Step 4 (Close-out): Start pump (OP-01) and confirm pressure. Accept: Pressure ≈ 2.1 bar within 30 s.
chunks.title: OP-06 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure EM-01 – High vibration / vibration trip (Emergency). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Respond to a vibration alarm or trip and protect the pump. When used: Vibration ≥ 4.5 mm/s or trip; rubbing/knocking noise. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-01 High vibration / vibration trip

chunks.text: EM-01 High vibration / vibration trip – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the standby unit (OP-03 step 2) to keep the flow going. Accept: Standby running; flow normal. Safety: If standby fails: go to EM-06. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop and isolate the vibrating unit (ISO steps). Accept: Unit isolated and locked. Step 3 (Inspection): Check coupling, base bolts, guard contact and debris; turn shaft by hand. Accept: Note: loose bolts / worn insert / rubbing / clogging. Step 4 (Inspection): Review the last 14 days of vibration and temperature trend on the tablet. Accept: Trend recorded in work order. Step 5 (Repair): Correct simple causes (tighten bolts, replace coupling insert PR-14, clear debris). Accept: Cause removed. Step 6 (Close-out): If bearing or impeller damage is suspected, raise corrective WO (PR-06 / PR-09) and inform engineer. Accept: WO raised; engineer informed.
chunks.title: EM-01 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure EM-02 – Mechanical seal leak (Emergency). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B. Purpose: Contain a seal leak and decide run / stop. When used: Leak > 5 drops/min, reservoir level falling, seal alarm (submersible). Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-02 Mechanical seal leak

chunks.text: EM-02 Mechanical seal leak – Step 1 (Inspection): Estimate leak rate and check the seal reservoir level. Accept: Leak rate and level recorded. Safety: Acidic liquid – face shield. Step 2 (Inspection): If ≤ 5 drops/min and level stable: keep running, check every round. Accept: Monitored. Step 3 (Isolation): If above limit: start standby, then stop and isolate leaking unit. Accept: Leaking unit isolated. Step 4 (Repair): Check spare seal stock; if 0 → emergency purchase (+30%, supplier list). Accept: Seal available or ordered. Step 5 (Repair): Replace seal (PR-07 transfer pump / PR-17 submersible). Accept: Seal replaced. Step 6 (Close-out): Record leak history; if 2nd seal failure in 12 months → repair-or-replace review. Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: EM-02 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure EM-03 – Pump clogging / low flow (Emergency). Equipment: P-201A/B, P-101A/B. Purpose: Clear a clogged pump or suction. When used: Flow drop > 20%, current change, overload trip. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-03 Pump clogging / low flow

chunks.text: EM-03 Pump clogging / low flow – Step 1 (Preparation): Start standby unit. Accept: Standby running. Step 2 (Isolation): Isolate the clogged unit (ISO steps); for submersible lift it out (PR-16). Accept: Isolated. Safety: Rags and fibre may hide sharp objects – cut-resistant gloves. Step 3 (Repair): Remove rags/fibre from impeller, strainer or suction. Accept: Impeller turns freely. Step 4 (Inspection): Check screens upstream for mesh holes or bypass (SV-01). Accept: Source of rags found. Step 5 (Close-out): Return to service (OP-05); report if screens let solids through. Accept: Flow restored.
chunks.title: EM-03 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure EM-04 – Cavitation / low suction (Emergency). Equipment: P-101A/B. Purpose: Stop cavitation damage when EQ level is low or suction is blocked. When used: Crackling noise, pressure fluctuating, EQ level low. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-04 Cavitation / low suction

chunks.text: EM-04 Cavitation / low suction – Step 1 (Inspection): Check EQ tank level and suction valve position. Accept: Level ≥ 30%; valve fully open. Step 2 (Repair): If level low: reduce pump flow (throttle discharge) or stop until level recovers. Accept: Noise stops. Step 3 (Repair): If level normal: clean suction strainer (SV-02). Accept: Strainer clean. Step 4 (Close-out): Record event; check impeller at next shutdown if cavitation lasted > 1 h. Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: EM-04 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure EM-05 – Motor overload trip (Emergency). Equipment: M-101A/B, P-201A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Find why a motor tripped on overload before restarting. When used: Thermal overload relay tripped. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-05 Motor overload trip

chunks.text: EM-05 Motor overload trip – Step 1 (Preparation): Start standby unit. Accept: Standby running. Step 2 (Isolation): Isolate the tripped unit (ISO steps). Accept: Isolated. Step 3 (Inspection): Turn shaft by hand; check for clogging or seizure. Accept: Shaft free / seized noted. Step 4 (Inspection): Check supply voltage on all 3 phases and overload setting. Accept: Phases balanced (±2%); setting = FLA. Safety: Electrician only for live tests. Step 5 (Inspection): Megger motor windings (electrician). Accept: ≥ 100 MΩ ready; < 5 MΩ → do not restart. Step 6 (Close-out): Reset only after cause is found; one reset attempt; else escalate. Accept: Cause recorded. Safety: Never keep resetting a trip.
chunks.title: EM-05 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure EM-06 – Standby fails to start (Emergency). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B, SC-101A/B. Purpose: Restore pumping when the standby will not start. When used: Standby does not start on demand. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-06 Standby fails to start

chunks.text: EM-06 Standby fails to start – Step 1 (Preparation): Inform shift supervisor and wastewater engineer immediately (pair may be down). Accept: Informed; time logged. Step 2 (Inspection): Check panel: breaker, overload, control fuse, selector switch. Accept: Electrical cause found / not found. Step 3 (Isolation): Isolate unit; turn shaft by hand. Accept: Seized → go to EM-09 escalation and PR-07; free → electrical check. Step 4 (Repair): If the duty unit can run safely at reduced load, keep it running while repair proceeds. Accept: Some flow kept. Step 5 (Close-out): Check when the unit last ran and was checked (rotation, standby check); record as lesson. Accept: Rotation/check gap recorded. Safety: Daily rotation prevents this.
chunks.title: EM-06 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure EM-07 – Motor overheating (Emergency). Equipment: M-101A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Prevent winding damage from high motor temperature. When used: Frame hot, IR > 80 °C on bearing, burning smell absent. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-07 Motor overheating

chunks.text: EM-07 Motor overheating – Step 1 (Inspection): Check fan cover and cooling fins for fibre/fat build-up. Accept: Clean / blocked noted. Step 2 (Inspection): Measure current on all phases. Accept: ≤ 105% FLA, balanced. Step 3 (Repair): If blocked: switch to standby, isolate, clean fan cover (PR fan check). Accept: Airflow restored. Step 4 (Close-out): If current high: check pump for clogging (EM-03). Accept: Cause recorded.
chunks.title: EM-07 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure EM-08 – Electrical fault / burning smell (Emergency). Equipment: Any motor or panel. Purpose: Make the area safe after an electrical fault. When used: Burning smell, smoke, earth-fault trip, sparks. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-08 Electrical fault / burning smell

chunks.text: EM-08 Electrical fault / burning smell – Step 1 (Isolation): Do not touch; switch off from the MCC; call electrician and supervisor. Accept: Supply off. Safety: Fire risk: CO2 extinguisher only; never water on live equipment. Step 2 (Preparation): Start standby unit if its circuit is separate and safe. Accept: Standby running. Step 3 (Inspection): Electrician inspects cable, terminal box and starter. Accept: Fault located. Safety: Only qualified electrician. Step 4 (Close-out): Megger before any restart; raise corrective WO. Accept: IR result recorded.
chunks.title: EM-08 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure EM-09 – Pump pair down – escalation and communication (Emergency). Equipment: PR-TRANSFER, PR-SUMP. Purpose: Limit production loss and avoid untreated bypass when both pumps of a pair are down. When used: Duty failed and standby not available. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-09 Pump pair down – escalation and communication

chunks.text: EM-09 Pump pair down – escalation and communication – Step 1 (Preparation): Call wastewater engineer, shift supervisor and production manager; start the incident on the tablet. Accept: Calls logged with time. Step 2 (Inspection): Read EQ (or sump) level and inflow; tablet shows buffer time. Accept: Buffer time known (EQ ≈ 2.5 h; sump ≈ 12 min). Step 3 (Repair): Ask production to curtail lines in order VCO+flour → DC → coconut water as level approaches high-high. Accept: Lines curtailed in order. Safety: Bypass only with engineer approval – RA 9275 fines. Step 4 (Repair): Repair the quicker unit first (EM-06 / EM-01); consider installing stored spare (OP-04). Accept: Repair under way. Step 5 (Close-out): When restored: restart lines; draft incident report on the tablet. Accept: Incident report drafted.
chunks.title: EM-09 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure EM-10 – Sump or EQ tank overflow risk (Emergency). Equipment: W01 sump, W04 EQ tank. Purpose: Prevent overflow and untreated discharge. When used: Level ≥ high alarm. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-10 Sump or EQ tank overflow risk

chunks.text: EM-10 Sump or EQ tank overflow risk – Step 1 (Inspection): Confirm level reading against the sight gauge (SV-05). Accept: Level confirmed. Step 2 (Repair): Check that the duty pump is running at full flow; start standby in parallel if allowed. Accept: Outflow ≥ inflow. Step 3 (Repair): Ask production to curtail washdown/CIP first, then lines (EM-09). Accept: Inflow reduced. Step 4 (Close-out): Record peak level and duration. Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: EM-10 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure EM-11 – Both screens down – forced shutdown (Emergency). Equipment: SC-101A/B. Purpose: Protect the biological stage when no screen is available. When used: Both screens failed or blinded. Prerequisites: None – act immediately. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves, safety glasses, face shield. Tools: Tablet, radio, clamp meter, vibration pen. Permits: Work permit if any part is opened. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: EM-11 Both screens down – forced shutdown

chunks.text: EM-11 Both screens down – forced shutdown – Step 1 (Preparation): Inform wastewater engineer and production manager: plant stop is required. Accept: Decision logged. Step 2 (Repair): Production stops lines in order; utilities continue. Accept: Inflow minimised. Step 3 (Repair): Repair the quicker screen first (SV-01 mesh, SV-03 vibrator motor). Accept: One screen restored. Step 4 (Close-out): Restart production after one screen is proven (OP-05). Accept: Production restarted; incident report drafted.
chunks.title: EM-11 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure PR-01 – Isolation and lockout/tagout (LOTO) – pumps (Pump repair). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B. Purpose: Make a pump safe before any work. When used: Before every repair. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Personal locks, tags, multimeter. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None.  FIG-07 Lockout/tagout points – breaker, valves, drain. Order of isolation; each worker applies own lock.
chunks.title: PR-01 Isolation and lockout/tagout (LOTO) – pumps

Accept: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA. Safety: Stand clear of coupling during start.
