chunks.text: PR-15 Shaft alignment (pump to motor) – Step 7 (Close-out): Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock. Accept: Work order complete; stock updated.
chunks.title: PR-15 steps 7–7

chunks.text: Procedure PR-16 – Submersible pump lifting, removal and reinstallation (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B, SP-P02. Purpose: Lift a submersible pump out of the sump for inspection or swap. When used: Clogging, seal alarm, swap with spare. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Chain block/hoist, lifting chain. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None. Why: The submersible sits under wastewater; it must be lifted out safely for any work. Do: Lift only by the chain/handle along the guide rails. Never: Lift by the power cable or stand under the load. Never: Enter the sump without a confined-space permit. FIG-02 Tsurumi submersible pump – cross-section, 11 numbered parts. Dry motor above an oil chamber between two mechanical seals; lift only by the chain. FIG-13 Lifting a submersible along the guide rails. Never lift by the cable; never stand under the load; no sump entry without permit.
chunks.title: PR-16 Submersible pump lifting, removal and reinstallation

chunks.text: PR-16 Submersible pump lifting, removal and reinstallation – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate the pump electrically (PR-01); confirm the partner pump is running. Accept: Isolated. Step 2 (Disassembly): Lift pump by its lifting chain on the guide rail; never by the cable. Accept: Pump out of sump. Safety: Never lift by the power cable; stand clear of load. Step 3 (Inspection): Rinse pump; inspect impeller, cable, strainer. Accept: Findings recorded. Safety: Wear gloves – raw wastewater. Step 4 (Reassembly): Lower pump along guide rail until seated on the discharge connector. Accept: Pump seated. Step 5 (Testing): Remove lock; start pump; check flow and current. Accept: Flow ≈ 48 m³/h; current ≈ 4.2 A. Step 6 (Close-out): Record work. Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: PR-16 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure PR-17 – Submersible seal and oil-chamber check (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B, SP-P02. Purpose: Check oil for water ingress and replace oil (and seal if needed). When used: Every 1,500 h or 6 months (plant: quarterly); seal alarm. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Oil container, megger. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-019, SPP-020, SPP-023. Why: The oil chamber protects the motor; water in the oil is the early warning of a failing lower seal. Do: Tsurumi interval: every 1,500 h or 6 months (plant: quarterly). Do: Use turbine oil ISO VG32 – quantity per Tsurumi manual (verify). Mistake: Topping up milky oil instead of replacing the seals. FIG-02 Tsurumi submersible pump – cross-section, 11 numbered parts. Dry motor above an oil chamber between two mechanical seals; lift only by the chain. FIG-16 Submersible oil check – clear, milky, water. Milky oil or water = seal failing. Illustrative example – not an actual photo.
chunks.title: PR-17 Submersible seal and oil-chamber check

chunks.text: PR-17 Submersible seal and oil-chamber check – Step 1 (Isolation): Lift pump (PR-16) and lay it on its side with oil plug up. Accept: Pump secured. Step 2 (Inspection): Drain a sample of oil; check colour. Accept: Clear = OK; milky or water drops = seal failing. Step 3 (Repair): Replace oil with turbine oil ISO VG32 to the specified quantity; new plug gasket. Accept: Oil level correct. Safety: Dispose of old oil per local rules. Step 4 (Repair): If oil was milky: replace upper and lower seals (workshop) and megger the motor. Accept: Seals replaced; IR ≥ 20 MΩ. Step 5 (Close-out): Reinstall pump (PR-16). Accept: Running normally.
chunks.title: PR-17 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure PR-18 – Submersible power cable check (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B. Purpose: Find cable damage before it causes an earth fault. When used: Quarterly; after earth-fault trip. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Megger, multimeter. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-022.  FIG-17 Power cable worn at the sump edge. Replace the cable and fit a guard at the edge. Illustrative example – not an actual photo.
chunks.title: PR-18 Submersible power cable check

chunks.text: PR-18 Submersible power cable check – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate pump electrically (PR-01). Accept: Isolated. Step 2 (Inspection): Inspect cable sheath along its length, especially at the sump edge. Accept: No cuts or abrasion. Step 3 (Inspection): Megger phases to earth. Accept: ≥ 20 MΩ new; repair needed at ≤ 10 MΩ. Step 4 (Repair): Fit cable guard at sump edge; replace damaged cable. Accept: Cable protected.
chunks.title: PR-18 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure PR-19 – Submersible flow-drop troubleshooting (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B. Purpose: Find why a submersible pump delivers less flow. When used: Flow down > 20% or current change. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Clamp meter, flow meter. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: As found.
chunks.title: PR-19 Submersible flow-drop troubleshooting

chunks.text: PR-19 Submersible flow-drop troubleshooting – Step 1 (Inspection): Compare flow and current with baseline (48 m³/h, 4.2 A). Accept: Deviation recorded. Step 2 (Inspection): Check rotation direction (phase sequence). Accept: Correct rotation. Step 3 (Inspection): Lift pump (PR-16); check for clogging and impeller wear. Accept: Cause found. Step 4 (Inspection): Check discharge check valve for sticking/backflow (SV-02). Accept: Valve OK / faulty. Step 5 (Close-out): Repair cause; record; if 2nd failure in 12 months → repair-or-replace review. Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: PR-19 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure SV-01 – Screen mesh replacement (Screen repair). Equipment: SC-101A/B. Purpose: Replace a torn or worn screen mesh panel. When used: Hole in mesh; fibre found downstream. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners, torque wrench. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-024, SPP-026. Why: A hole in the mesh lets fibre reach the EQ tank and the transfer pumps (seal and impeller damage). Do: Switch the flow to the other screen first (SV-08). Do: Tension the clamps evenly. Mistake: Over-tensioning – tears start at the clamp line. FIG-04 Vibrating screen – parts. Mesh panel, mounts, vibrator motors, solids chute, clamps. FIG-18 Screen mesh tear. Tears often start at the clamp line; solids pass to the EQ tank. Illustrative example – not an actual photo.
chunks.title: SV-01 Screen mesh replacement

chunks.text: SV-01 Screen mesh replacement – Step 1 (Preparation): Switch flow to the other screen; confirm it is running. Accept: Other screen carrying load. Step 2 (Isolation): Isolate vibrator motors of the screen (LOTO). Accept: Isolated. Step 3 (Disassembly): Release clamps; remove old mesh panel. Accept: Panel removed. Safety: Sharp mesh edges – cut-resistant gloves. Step 4 (Repair): Fit new panel; tension clamps evenly. Accept: Even tension; no gaps at edges. Safety: Over-tension causes tears at clamp line. Step 5 (Testing): Run screen 15 min; check for leaks of solids at edges. Accept: No bypass of solids. Step 6 (Close-out): Update mesh stock; reorder if below minimum. Accept: Stock updated.
chunks.title: SV-01 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure SV-02 – Check valve inspection and replacement (Valve repair). Equipment: Discharge check valves of P-101A/B, P-201A/B. Purpose: Stop backflow through a failed check valve. When used: Reverse rotation; backflow; banging. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners, lifting gear. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-029, SPP-030, SPP-031. Why: A failed check valve lets water flow back and spins the pump backwards. Do: Isolate both sides and drain before opening. Do: After repair, stop the pump and confirm the shaft stays still. Mistake: Opening the valve cover under pressure. FIG-06 Swing check valve – flapper and signs of failure. A failed flapper lets water flow back and spins the pump backwards.
chunks.title: SV-02 Check valve inspection and replacement
chunks.group: Discharge check valves of P-101A/B, P-201A/B

chunks.text: SV-02 Check valve inspection and replacement – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate pump and close isolation valves both sides (PR-01). Accept: Section isolated and drained. Step 2 (Disassembly): Open valve cover; inspect flapper, hinge pin and seat. Accept: Wear recorded. Step 3 (Repair): Replace flapper/seat kit or whole valve. Accept: New parts fitted. Step 4 (Testing): Return to service; stop pump and confirm no reverse rotation. Accept: Shaft stays still after stop.
chunks.title: SV-02 steps 1–4
chunks.group: Discharge check valves of P-101A/B, P-201A/B

chunks.text: Procedure SV-03 – Isolation valve repair (Valve repair). Equipment: Suction/discharge gate or butterfly valves. Purpose: Restore tight shut-off of an isolation valve. When used: Valve passes when closed; stiff operation. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: Gland packing / seat kit.
chunks.title: SV-03 Isolation valve repair

chunks.text: SV-03 Isolation valve repair – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate the line section (upstream and downstream). Accept: Section isolated. Step 2 (Repair): Repack gland or replace seat per valve type. Accept: Valve operates smoothly. Step 3 (Testing): Close valve and check for passing. Accept: No passing.
chunks.title: SV-03 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-04 – Pressure gauge replacement (Instrument). Equipment: Discharge gauges of P-101A/B. Purpose: Replace a stuck, fogged or wrong gauge. When used: Gauge stuck/fogged; reading differs from expected. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners, PTFE tape. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-032.
chunks.title: SV-04 Pressure gauge replacement

chunks.text: SV-04 Pressure gauge replacement – Step 1 (Isolation): Close gauge isolation cock. Accept: Gauge isolated. Safety: Pressure in line – open slowly later. Step 2 (Repair): Replace gauge (0–4 bar, glycerine-filled). Accept: Gauge fitted. Step 3 (Testing): Open cock; compare with expected ≈ 2.1 bar when running. Accept: Reading plausible.
chunks.title: SV-04 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-05 – Level transmitter check against sight gauge (Instrument). Equipment: EQ tank, sump level transmitters. Purpose: Confirm the level reading is correct. When used: Monthly; level alarm doubtful. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Tablet. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None.
chunks.title: SV-05 Level transmitter check against sight gauge

chunks.text: SV-05 Level transmitter check against sight gauge – Step 1 (Inspection): Read level on panel/tablet and on sight gauge at the same time. Accept: Difference recorded. Step 2 (Inspection): Difference ≤ 5% of span is OK. Accept: Within 5%. Step 3 (Close-out): If > 5%: raise WO for calibration. Accept: WO raised.
chunks.title: SV-05 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-06 – Suction strainer cleaning (Valve repair). Equipment: P-101A/B suction strainers. Purpose: Remove debris that restricts suction. When used: Low suction pressure; cavitation; monthly. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-033 (if damaged).
chunks.title: SV-06 Suction strainer cleaning

chunks.text: SV-06 Suction strainer cleaning – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate pump (PR-01) and close strainer valves. Accept: Isolated. Step 2 (Repair): Remove basket; clean; inspect for holes. Accept: Basket clean and intact. Step 3 (Testing): Refit with new gasket; return pump to service. Accept: Normal suction.
chunks.title: SV-06 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-07 – Screen cleaning (cream / oil blinding) (Screen repair). Equipment: SC-101A/B. Purpose: Remove fat and coconut cream that blind the mesh. When used: Every shift; mesh partly blinded. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Low-pressure hot water hose, brush. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-034.  FIG-04 Vibrating screen – parts. Mesh panel, mounts, vibrator motors, solids chute, clamps.
chunks.title: SV-07 Screen cleaning (cream / oil blinding)

chunks.text: SV-07 Screen cleaning (cream / oil blinding) – Step 1 (Preparation): Switch flow to the other screen if mesh is fully blinded. Accept: Flow on other screen. Step 2 (Repair): Spray hot water and food-safe degreaser; brush mesh. Accept: Mesh open. Safety: Do not use high-pressure jet on mesh. Step 3 (Close-out): Return screen to service; note if blinding repeats within the shift (inform production). Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: SV-07 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-08 – Screen duty changeover (Screen repair). Equipment: SC-101A/B. Purpose: Move the flow from one screen to the other. When used: Daily rotation; screen fault. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: None. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None.  FIG-04 Vibrating screen – parts. Mesh panel, mounts, vibrator motors, solids chute, clamps.
chunks.title: SV-08 Screen duty changeover

chunks.text: SV-08 Screen duty changeover – Step 1 (Preparation): Start vibrator motors of the standby screen. Accept: Screen vibrating normally. Step 2 (Repair): Open inlet gate to standby screen; close inlet to the other screen. Accept: Flow on new screen; no overflow. Step 3 (Close-out): Stop vibrators of the idle screen; log changeover. Accept: Logged.
chunks.title: SV-08 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure SV-09 – Vibrating screen isolation mounts replacement (Screen repair). Equipment: SC-101A/B. Purpose: Replace cracked springs/rubber mounts. When used: Rattling; uneven vibration. Prerequisites: Partner screen/valve path available. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Jacks, spanners. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-025.  FIG-04 Vibrating screen – parts. Mesh panel, mounts, vibrator motors, solids chute, clamps.
chunks.title: SV-09 Vibrating screen isolation mounts replacement

chunks.text: SV-09 Vibrating screen isolation mounts replacement – Step 1 (Preparation): Move flow to other screen (SV-08); isolate vibrators (LOTO). Accept: Isolated. Step 2 (Repair): Jack screen frame; replace all mounts as a set. Accept: New mounts fitted. Safety: Support frame before removing mounts. Step 3 (Testing): Run screen; check even motion and noise. Accept: Normal motion.
chunks.title: SV-09 steps 1–3

chunks.text: Procedure PR-20 – Transfer pump complete overhaul (workshop) (Pump repair). Equipment: P-101A/B, SP-P01. Purpose: Restore a transfer pump to as-new condition by replacing all wear parts. When used: Repair-or-replace result = Repair after major failure; spare pump refurbishment. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Full tool kit, bearing heater, pullers, micrometers, seal gauge, torque wrench, chain block. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-001, SPP-002, SPP-003, SPP-004, SPP-005, SPP-006, SPP-007, SPP-008, SPP-009. Why: Restores the pump to as-new condition when the repair-or-replace review says Repair. Do: Lay out parts in order, photograph as found, measure everything before cleaning. Do: Replace all wear parts in one go – bearings, seals, sleeve, wear ring, gaskets, coupling insert. Mistake: Re-using worn parts 'because they look OK' – measure against limits. FIG-01 KSB transfer pump – cross-section, 14 numbered parts. Seals 6 and 7 sit in the lubricant reservoir (8); the casing (1) stays on the pipes.
chunks.title: PR-20 Transfer pump complete overhaul (workshop)

chunks.text: PR-20 Transfer pump complete overhaul (workshop) – Step 1 (Preparation): Get work order, permit and this procedure on the tablet; brief the crew on hazards (440 V motor supply; pressure in discharge line; liquid in casing). Accept: Permit signed; crew briefed. Safety: Only trained (authorized) persons apply locks. Step 2 (Isolation): Notify the shift supervisor and operator; confirm the partner unit is running or production is informed. Accept: Partner running or supervisor approval recorded. Safety: Do not isolate both units of a pair without engineer approval. Step 3 (Isolation): Stop the pump at the local panel; open and lock the MCC breaker; attach personal lock and tag. Accept: Breaker OFF and locked; tag shows name, date, reason. Safety: Each worker applies own lock. Step 4 (Isolation): Close and lock suction and discharge isolation valves; open casing drain to release pressure. Accept: Gauge reads 0 bar; drain flowing then stops. Safety: Wastewater is acidic (pH ~5): gloves, face shield. Step 5 (Isolation): Try to start from local and remote stations (try-out); return switches to OFF. Accept: Unit does not start. Safety: Never skip the try-out step. Step 6 (Disassembly): Remove the pump from site (PR-02) and move it to the workshop; record nameplate and as-found condition with photos. Accept: Pump on bench; photos taken. Safety: Lifting plan for transport.
chunks.title: PR-20 steps 1–6

chunks.text: PR-20 Transfer pump complete overhaul (workshop) – Step 7 (Disassembly): Drain the seal reservoir; remove impeller (PR-09), casing cover, seals (PR-07) and shaft sleeve (PR-12). Accept: Parts laid out in order and labelled. Step 8 (Disassembly): Remove coupling hub, bearing covers and bearings (PR-06); remove shaft from the bearing bracket. Accept: Shaft free. Step 9 (Inspection): Measure shaft run-out between centres and check bearing seats and keyways. Accept: Run-out within KSB limit (verify); no cracks. Step 10 (Inspection): Inspect casing and cover for erosion, corrosion and cracks; measure wear-ring gap. Accept: Record values; replace ring if above limit. Step 11 (Repair): Clean all parts; replace all wear parts listed (bearings, seals, sleeve, wear ring, gaskets, coupling insert; impeller if worn). Accept: Only new or within-limit parts used. Step 12 (Reassembly): Fit shaft and new bearings into the bracket; fit sleeve, seals (setting dimension), cover and impeller; torque nut. Accept: Shaft turns freely; seal set to KSB dimension.
chunks.title: PR-20 steps 7–12

chunks.text: PR-20 Transfer pump complete overhaul (workshop) – Step 13 (Reassembly): Fill the seal reservoir; fit a new casing gasket; reinstall at site (PR-03) and align (PR-15). Accept: Alignment within limits. Step 14 (Testing): Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock). Accept: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners. Safety: Warn everyone before re-energizing. Step 15 (Testing): Start the pump and record readings; Run 1 h, then do a performance check (PR-25). Accept: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA. Safety: Stand clear of coupling during start. Step 16 (Close-out): Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock. Accept: Work order complete; stock updated.
chunks.title: PR-20 steps 13–16

chunks.text: Procedure PR-21 – Commissioning a new or rebuilt transfer pump (Pump repair). Equipment: P-101A/B, SP-P01. Purpose: Check a new or rebuilt pump before it is accepted into service. When used: New unit installed (e.g. P-101A, Jun 2026); after overhaul. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Alignment kit, megger, clamp meter, vibration pen, IR thermometer, tablet. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None. Why: A new pump only proves itself with checks and a baseline; the baseline is used for every later comparison. Do: Megger before first start; bump-start to check rotation. Do: Save the 4-hour run readings and performance check as the new baseline. Mistake: Skipping pipe-strain check – flanges must line up without force.
chunks.title: PR-21 Commissioning a new or rebuilt transfer pump

chunks.text: PR-21 Commissioning a new or rebuilt transfer pump – Step 1 (Preparation): Check the delivery against the order: model, size, impeller, seal type, motor rating, documents and manual. Accept: Matches order; manual on file. Step 2 (Preparation): Check the seal reservoir is filled (factory fill) and the shaft turns by hand. Accept: Level normal; shaft free. Step 3 (Inspection): Megger the motor before first start. Accept: ≥ 100 MΩ at 500 V DC (plant rule). Safety: Electrician only. Step 4 (Inspection): Check soft foot (PR-04), pipe strain (flanges align without force) and alignment (PR-15). Accept: All within limits. Step 5 (Testing): Bump-start (1–2 s) to confirm rotation direction. Accept: Rotation matches arrow on casing. Safety: Keep clear of coupling. Step 6 (Testing): Prime and vent (OP-06); start (OP-01); run 4 h with readings every hour. Accept: Vibration < 2.8 mm/s; bearings < 80 °C and stable; current ≤ 12.8 A; no seal leak.
chunks.title: PR-21 steps 1–6

chunks.text: PR-21 Commissioning a new or rebuilt transfer pump – Step 7 (Testing): Do a performance check (PR-25) and save the results as the baseline. Accept: Within 5% of the expected duty point (assumed). Step 8 (Close-out): Add or update the asset in the Equipment_Register (install date, serial, baseline); attach QR tag; set PM schedule start. Accept: Asset record complete; QR scans correctly.
chunks.title: PR-21 steps 7–8

chunks.text: Procedure PR-22 – Preservation and storage of a spare pump (Pump repair). Equipment: SP-P01, SP-P02. Purpose: Keep a stored spare pump ready to install at short notice. When used: On entry into store; monthly and quarterly storage checks. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Hand tools, desiccant bags, plastic covers, megger (motors), tablet. Permits: None. Parts: Desiccant, rust preventive.
chunks.title: PR-22 Preservation and storage of a spare pump

chunks.text: PR-22 Preservation and storage of a spare pump – Step 1 (Preparation): Clean and dry the pump; drain any liquid from the casing. Accept: Pump clean and dry. Step 2 (Repair): Coat exposed machined surfaces (shaft end, flange faces) with rust preventive; blank off flanges. Accept: Surfaces coated; flanges covered. Step 3 (Repair): Place desiccant in the casing openings; cover the unit; store indoors, off the floor, away from vibration. Accept: Stored in the assigned location. Step 4 (Inspection): Monthly: turn the shaft by hand 5 turns and stop at a different position; check covers and desiccant. Accept: Shaft turns freely; desiccant dry. Step 5 (Inspection): Check the seal reservoir level (transfer pump) or oil level (submersible). Accept: Level normal. Step 6 (Close-out): Record the check in Spare_Readiness; set the status Ready or Not ready. Accept: Record saved; next due date shown. Safety: A Not ready spare must raise a work order.
chunks.title: PR-22 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure PR-23 – Submersible impeller replacement and full service (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B, SP-P02. Purpose: Replace a worn submersible impeller and service the wet end. When used: Flow drop not fixed by cleaning; impeller worn; quarterly finding. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Spanners, puller, feeler gauges, megger, torque wrench. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-021, SPP-019, SPP-020, SPP-023. Why: A worn submersible impeller lowers flow so the sump fills faster. Do: Check the oil chamber at the same time (PR-17). Do: Megger motor and cable before reinstalling: ≥ 20 MΩ. Mistake: Not setting the impeller-to-suction-cover clearance (verify in Tsurumi manual). FIG-02 Tsurumi submersible pump – cross-section, 11 numbered parts. Dry motor above an oil chamber between two mechanical seals; lift only by the chain. FIG-15 Worn vs new impeller. Thinner vane tips and grit grooves mean less flow and head. Illustrative example – not an actual photo.
chunks.title: PR-23 Submersible impeller replacement and full service

chunks.text: PR-23 Submersible impeller replacement and full service – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate electrically (PR-01); lift the pump out (PR-16); wash it down. Accept: Pump on stand, clean. Safety: Raw wastewater – gloves, face shield. Step 2 (Disassembly): Remove the strainer/suction cover; hold the impeller and remove the impeller bolt; pull the impeller. Accept: Impeller removed; key kept. Step 3 (Inspection): Check the impeller, suction cover and lower seal for wear and damage. Accept: Wear recorded. Step 4 (Repair): Check oil chamber (PR-17); replace seals if oil is milky. Accept: Oil clear or seals replaced. Step 5 (Reassembly): Fit the new impeller and key; torque bolt; set the impeller-to-suction-cover clearance. Accept: Clearance per Tsurumi manual (verify). Step 6 (Testing): Megger the motor and cable; reinstall (PR-16); check flow and current. Accept: IR ≥ 20 MΩ; flow ≈ 48 m³/h; current ≈ 4.2 A.
chunks.title: PR-23 steps 1–6

chunks.text: PR-23 Submersible impeller replacement and full service – Step 7 (Close-out): Record parts and readings; update stock. Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: PR-23 steps 7–7

chunks.text: Procedure PR-24 – Submersible guide rail and discharge connector check (Pump repair). Equipment: P-201A/B. Purpose: Make sure the submersible seats correctly on its discharge connector. When used: Annually; leak at the connector; pump does not seat. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Lifting gear, torch, spanners. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: Connector gasket.  FIG-13 Lifting a submersible along the guide rails. Never lift by the cable; never stand under the load; no sump entry without permit.
chunks.title: PR-24 Submersible guide rail and discharge connector check

chunks.text: PR-24 Submersible guide rail and discharge connector check – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate and lift the pump out (PR-16); lower sump level as far as possible. Accept: Pump out; connector visible. Safety: Confined-space rules if entry is needed – do not enter without permit. Step 2 (Inspection): Inspect the guide rails for bending and corrosion and the brackets for loose bolts. Accept: Rails straight; bolts tight. Step 3 (Inspection): Inspect the discharge connector seat and gasket for wear or debris. Accept: Seat clean; gasket intact. Step 4 (Repair): Replace the gasket; clean the seat; re-tighten brackets. Accept: Done. Step 5 (Testing): Lower the pump along the rails; start and check for leaks or noise at the connector. Accept: Seats smoothly; no leak noise; flow normal.
chunks.title: PR-24 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure PR-25 – Pump performance check (flow, pressure, power) (Pump repair). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B. Purpose: Compare a pump's running point with its curve to find wear early. When used: Quarterly; after overhaul or commissioning; when flow seems low. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Flow meter or tank-level timing, calibrated pressure gauge, clamp meter, tablet. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: PR-25 Pump performance check (flow, pressure, power)

chunks.text: PR-25 Pump performance check (flow, pressure, power) – Step 1 (Preparation): Make sure the pump runs alone on its line with a stable level. Accept: Steady conditions for 10 min. Step 2 (Inspection): Record flow (meter, or EQ level change × tank area over a timed period with inflow known). Accept: Flow recorded (m³/h). Step 3 (Inspection): Record suction level and discharge pressure; work out the head. Accept: Head recorded (m). Step 4 (Inspection): Record motor current and voltage; work out the input power. Accept: Power recorded (kW). Step 5 (Inspection): Plot the point against the pump curve (or the baseline from commissioning). Accept: Flow or head drop > 10% at the same conditions = wear (assumed rule). Step 6 (Close-out): If below limit: plan impeller/wear-ring work (PR-09, PR-11, PR-23); save results to the asset history. Accept: Action planned; result saved.
chunks.title: PR-25 steps 1–6

chunks.text: Procedure PR-26 – Routine pump inspection (monthly / quarterly checklist) (Pump repair). Equipment: P-101A/B, P-201A/B. Purpose: Find small problems during normal running before they become failures. When used: Monthly (all pumps); quarterly extra items. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat, face shield, rubber apron. Tools: Vibration pen, IR thermometer, clamp meter, torch, tablet. Permits: None. Parts: None.
chunks.title: PR-26 Routine pump inspection (monthly / quarterly checklist)

chunks.text: PR-26 Routine pump inspection (monthly / quarterly checklist) – Step 1 (Inspection): Listen for unusual noise; look for leaks at seal, joints and drains. Accept: No new noise or leak. Step 2 (Inspection): Take vibration (DE/NDE) and bearing temperatures; compare with last month. Accept: Below alarm; no rise > 1 mm/s. Step 3 (Inspection): Check the seal reservoir level and colour (transfer pumps). Accept: Level normal; lubricant clear. Step 4 (Inspection): Check base bolts, coupling guard and pipe supports. Accept: Tight and in place. Step 5 (Inspection): Submersibles: check flow and current vs baseline; look at the cable at the sump edge. Accept: Within 10% of baseline; cable undamaged. Step 6 (Inspection): Quarterly extra: performance check (PR-25), alignment check (PR-15), oil chamber (PR-17). Accept: Done and recorded.
chunks.title: PR-26 steps 1–6

chunks.text: PR-26 Routine pump inspection (monthly / quarterly checklist) – Step 7 (Close-out): Enter results; anything abnormal raises a work order automatically. Accept: Inspection saved.
chunks.title: PR-26 steps 7–7

chunks.text: Procedure MO-01 – Motor insulation resistance (megger) test (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, SP-M01, VM-101A/B, SP-VM01, P-201A/B. Purpose: Check winding insulation before it fails. When used: Semi-annual; before first start of a spare; after flooding or a trip. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Insulation tester (500 V DC), thermometer, multimeter. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: None. Why: Insulation falls slowly with moisture and dirt; testing finds it before an earth fault or burnt winding. Do: Test at about 500 V DC for motors up to 1 kV; record the winding temperature with the result (IEEE 43). Do: Compare with the last result – a big drop matters even above 100 MΩ. Never: Test a motor that is not locked out, or touch the leads before discharging. FIG-14 Insulation (megger) test hook-up. 500 V DC to earth for 1 min; ≥ 100 MΩ Ready, < 5 MΩ Not ready.
chunks.title: MO-01 Motor insulation resistance (megger) test

chunks.text: MO-01 Motor insulation resistance (megger) test – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Preparation): Disconnect the motor cables at the terminal box (or test from the starter with cable included – note which). Accept: Leads disconnected and marked. Step 5 (Inspection): Apply 500 V DC phase-to-earth for 1 minute; record reading and winding temperature. Accept: Reading recorded with temperature. Safety: Discharge the winding to earth after each test. Step 6 (Inspection): Optional: read again at 10 minutes and work out the polarization index (10-min ÷ 1-min). Accept: PI recorded.
chunks.title: MO-01 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-01 Motor insulation resistance (megger) test – Step 7 (Inspection): Compare with plant rule and the last result. Accept: ≥ 100 MΩ = Ready; 5–100 MΩ = watch / dry out; < 5 MΩ = Not ready. Step 8 (Close-out): Reconnect (correct phase order), close terminal box, remove locks; record result in the tablet. Accept: Result saved; trend updated.
chunks.title: MO-01 steps 7–8

chunks.text: Procedure MO-02 – Motor bearing greasing (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Replace degraded grease in regreasable motor bearings. When used: Monthly plant interval (verify against motor nameplate); after bearing noise in rounds. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Grease gun (marked for this grease only), clean cloths, IR thermometer. Permits: None (motor running) – keep clear of coupling. Parts: SPP-018. Why: Old grease loses its oil and collects dirt; fresh grease keeps the bearings cool. Bearing failure is the most common motor failure. Do: Check the lubrication plate: grease type, quantity, interval. Sealed bearings are NOT greased. Do: Open the drain plug and run the motor so old grease can purge. Mistake: Over-greasing – too much grease churns and overheats the bearing. Never: Mix grease types; use a dirty nipple or gun. FIG-03 Motor – cross-section with grease nipples and drain plugs. Grease nipples (green) at DE and NDE; open the drain plug while greasing.
chunks.title: MO-02 Motor bearing greasing

chunks.text: MO-02 Motor bearing greasing – Step 1 (Preparation): Check the nameplate/lubrication plate: grease type, quantity per bearing, interval. Sealed (2Z/2RS) bearings are NOT greased. Accept: Motor is regreasable; values known. Safety: Never mix grease types. Step 2 (Preparation): Wipe the grease nipples and the gun nozzle clean. Accept: Nipples clean. Safety: Dirt pushed into a bearing shortens its life. Step 3 (Repair): Remove the grease drain plug (if fitted). Accept: Drain open. Step 4 (Repair): Add the specified quantity slowly to the DE bearing, then the NDE bearing (count gun strokes – 1 stroke ≈ value marked on gun). Accept: Quantity per nameplate (verify). Safety: Over-greasing overheats the bearing. Step 5 (Testing): Run the motor 15–30 min with the drain open so old grease can purge, then refit plug. Accept: Old grease purged; plug refitted. Safety: Keep clear of rotating shaft. Step 6 (Testing): Check bearing temperature after 1 h. Accept: Temperature back to normal (< 80 °C); short rise after greasing is normal.
chunks.title: MO-02 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-02 Motor bearing greasing – Step 7 (Close-out): Record date, grease used and quantity. Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: MO-02 steps 7–7

chunks.text: Procedure MO-03 – Motor bearing replacement (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, SP-M01. Purpose: Replace worn motor bearings. When used: High vibration/temperature at motor bearings; noise. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Bearing puller, induction heater, torque wrench, soft mallet. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-011, SPP-012, SPP-018. Why: Worn motor bearings cause noise, vibration and heat, and can let the rotor rub the stator. Do: Mark end shields before removing; protect the winding when pulling the rotor. Do: Heat new bearings with an induction heater. Mistake: Forgetting to megger and re-align after the job. FIG-03 Motor – cross-section with grease nipples and drain plugs. Grease nipples (green) at DE and NDE; open the drain plug while greasing. FIG-10 Fitting a bearing with an induction heater. Heat to about 110 °C and push to the shoulder; never use a flame or hammer the outer ring.
chunks.title: MO-03 Motor bearing replacement

chunks.text: MO-03 Motor bearing replacement – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Disassembly): Disconnect cables; uncouple; move the motor to the workshop. Accept: Motor on bench. Safety: Lifting: use eyebolt. Step 5 (Disassembly): Remove fan cover and fan; mark end shields; remove end shields and rotor. Accept: Rotor out without touching the winding. Safety: Protect winding from damage. Step 6 (Disassembly): Pull bearings with a puller. Accept: Shaft seats undamaged.
chunks.title: MO-03 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-03 Motor bearing replacement – Step 7 (Repair): Heat new bearings (≈ 110 °C) and fit to the shoulder; fill with grease if open type. Accept: Bearings seated. Safety: Heat-resistant gloves. Step 8 (Reassembly): Refit rotor, end shields (to marks), fan and cover; turn shaft by hand. Accept: Turns freely. Step 9 (Testing): Megger (MO-01); reinstall, align (PR-15), test run (OP-05). Accept: IR ≥ 100 MΩ; vibration < 2.8 mm/s.
chunks.title: MO-03 steps 7–9

chunks.text: Procedure MO-04 – Cooling fan and fan cover cleaning (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Keep motor cooling air flowing. When used: Monthly with greasing; fibre/fat build-up seen. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Brush, scraper, compressed air (low pressure), cloths. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-014 (if damaged).  FIG-03 Motor – cross-section with grease nipples and drain plugs. Grease nipples (green) at DE and NDE; open the drain plug while greasing.
chunks.title: MO-04 Cooling fan and fan cover cleaning

chunks.text: MO-04 Cooling fan and fan cover cleaning – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Disassembly): Remove fan cover. Accept: Cover off. Step 5 (Repair): Clean fan, cover grille and frame fins of fibre and fat. Accept: Air paths clear. Safety: Do not wash with water jets. Step 6 (Inspection): Check fan blades for cracks and the cover for dents touching the fan. Accept: No damage.
chunks.title: MO-04 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-04 Cooling fan and fan cover cleaning – Step 7 (Reassembly): Refit cover; turn shaft by hand. Accept: No rubbing. Step 8 (Testing): Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock). Accept: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners. Safety: Warn everyone before re-energizing. Step 9 (Testing): Start the motor and record readings; Run 30 min: frame temperature normal. Accept: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA. Safety: Stand clear of coupling during start. Step 10 (Close-out): Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock. Accept: Work order complete; stock updated.
chunks.title: MO-04 steps 7–10

chunks.text: Procedure MO-05 – Terminal box, cable gland and connection check (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Find loose or overheated connections and stop water entry. When used: Semi-annual with megger; after tightening found in rounds. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Insulated tools, torque screwdriver, IR thermometer. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-015.
chunks.title: MO-05 Terminal box, cable gland and connection check

chunks.text: MO-05 Terminal box, cable gland and connection check – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Inspection): Open the terminal box; look for burn marks, discoloured lugs, moisture. Accept: Clean and dry. Step 5 (Repair): Re-torque terminal nuts to the motor maker's value. Accept: Torque per maker (verify). Step 6 (Repair): Check the gland seals the cable; replace the gasket if hard or cracked. Accept: Gland tight; gasket good. Safety: Wet area – water entry causes earth faults.
chunks.title: MO-05 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-05 Terminal box, cable gland and connection check – Step 7 (Reassembly): Close box with all screws. Accept: Box sealed. Step 8 (Testing): Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock). Accept: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners. Safety: Warn everyone before re-energizing. Step 9 (Testing): Start the motor and record readings; Run 15 min: current balanced. Accept: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA. Safety: Stand clear of coupling during start. Step 10 (Close-out): Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock. Accept: Work order complete; stock updated.
chunks.title: MO-05 steps 7–10

chunks.text: Procedure MO-06 – Overload relay and contactor check (Motor). Equipment: Starters of M-101A/B, P-201A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Make sure motors are protected and switch cleanly. When used: Semi-annual; after an overload trip. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Multimeter, clamp meter, contact cleaner. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-016, SPP-017.
chunks.title: MO-06 Overload relay and contactor check

chunks.text: MO-06 Overload relay and contactor check – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate the starter from its supply (LOTO at the incomer); verify 0 V. Accept: 0 V. Safety: Electrician only. Step 2 (Inspection): Check overload setting against motor full-load current (M-101: 12.8 A). Accept: Setting = FLA (not higher). Safety: Never raise the setting to stop nuisance trips. Step 3 (Inspection): Inspect contactor contacts and coil terminals for pitting, heat marks. Accept: Contacts good. Step 4 (Repair): Replace worn contactor or overload relay. Accept: Replaced. Step 5 (Testing): Restore supply; start motor; measure current on 3 phases. Accept: Balanced within 10%; ≤ FLA.
chunks.title: MO-06 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure MO-07 – Motor replacement and rotation check (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, SP-M01. Purpose: Swap a failed motor with the spare and confirm correct rotation. When used: Motor failure; insulation < 5 MΩ; workshop repair needed. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Chain block, alignment kit, megger, phase rotation meter. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: Coupling insert.
chunks.title: MO-07 Motor replacement and rotation check

chunks.text: MO-07 Motor replacement and rotation check – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Disassembly): Disconnect and mark cables; uncouple; remove the failed motor. Accept: Motor removed; cables marked. Step 5 (Preparation): Check the spare: Spare_Readiness Ready; megger ≥ 100 MΩ. Accept: Spare ready. Step 6 (Repair): Install spare; fit coupling hub; connect cables in the marked order. Accept: Installed.
chunks.title: MO-07 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-07 Motor replacement and rotation check – Step 7 (Repair): Align to pump (PR-15). Accept: Within limits. Step 8 (Testing): Bump-start (1–2 s) uncoupled or with guard on; check rotation against the pump arrow. Accept: Correct rotation. Safety: Wrong rotation can unscrew an impeller. Step 9 (Testing): Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock). Accept: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners. Safety: Warn everyone before re-energizing. Step 10 (Testing): Start the motor and record readings; Run 30 min: flow, pressure, current, vibration and bearing temperature normal. Accept: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA. Safety: Stand clear of coupling during start. Step 11 (Close-out): Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock. Accept: Work order complete; stock updated.
chunks.title: MO-07 steps 7–11

chunks.text: Procedure MO-08 – Drying out a damp motor (Motor). Equipment: SP-M01, M-101A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Recover insulation resistance after moisture entry. When used: IR between 5 and 100 MΩ, or < 5 MΩ after flooding/condensation. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Drying oven or heater lamps, megger, thermometer. Permits: None. Parts: Desiccant. Why: A damp winding can recover if dried properly; burning it out costs a rewind. Do: Heat gently, keep below about 90 °C, megger every 4 h. Do: Accept only when readings stop rising and are ≥ 100 MΩ at the same temperature. Story: SP-M01 dropped to 3.2 MΩ in Aug 2025 and recovered to 450 MΩ after drying.
chunks.title: MO-08 Drying out a damp motor

chunks.text: MO-08 Drying out a damp motor – Step 1 (Isolation): Isolate and remove the motor to the workshop (or stores). Accept: Motor in workshop. Step 2 (Repair): Open terminal box and drain plugs; heat the winding gently (oven or lamps) – keep below about 90 °C. Accept: Temperature controlled. Safety: Do not overheat the winding. Step 3 (Inspection): Megger every 4 h and record; continue until readings stop rising. Accept: Readings rising then steady. Step 4 (Inspection): Accept when ≥ 100 MΩ (corrected to the same temperature). Accept: Ready. Step 5 (Close-out): Store with silica gel and cover (MO-10); update Spare_Readiness. Accept: Status Ready.
chunks.title: MO-08 steps 1–5

chunks.text: Procedure MO-09 – Vibrator motor service (Motor). Equipment: VM-101A/B, SP-VM01. Purpose: Keep both vibrator motors of a screen matched and in good condition. When used: Semi-annual; noise, uneven screen motion, high current. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Torque wrench, clamp meter, megger. Permits: Work permit; LOTO. Parts: SPP-027, SPP-028. Why: The two vibrator motors make the linear screen motion only when matched and turning in opposite directions. Do: Set both eccentric weights equal on both motors and both ends. Do: After work, check opposite rotation and balanced current (≈ 3.2 A each). Mistake: Changing one motor's weights only – the screen twists and welds crack. FIG-05 Vibrator motors – opposite rotation, equal weights. Both motors turn in opposite directions; eccentric weights set equal.
chunks.title: MO-09 Vibrator motor service

chunks.text: MO-09 Vibrator motor service – Step 1 (Preparation): Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally. Accept: Partner running. Step 2 (Isolation): Stop the vibrator motors; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock). Accept: Breaker OFF, locked, tagged. Step 3 (Isolation): Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals. Accept: Does not start; 0 V all phases. Safety: Test the meter on a live source first. Step 4 (Inspection): Remove eccentric weight covers; check both weights are at the same setting on both motors and both shaft ends. Accept: Settings equal. Safety: Unequal settings twist the screen. Step 5 (Inspection): Check mounting bolts for torque and frame welds for cracks. Accept: Tight; no cracks. Step 6 (Repair): Grease bearings if regreasable (MO-02); replace bearing set if noisy. Accept: Done.
chunks.title: MO-09 steps 1–6

chunks.text: MO-09 Vibrator motor service – Step 7 (Reassembly): Refit weight covers with new gaskets. Accept: Sealed. Step 8 (Testing): Start; confirm the two motors turn in opposite directions; measure current. Accept: Opposite rotation; current ≈ 3.2 A each, balanced.
chunks.title: MO-09 steps 7–8

chunks.text: Procedure MO-10 – Spare motor storage and preservation (Motor). Equipment: SP-M01, SP-VM01. Purpose: Keep a stored motor ready to install. When used: On entry to store; monthly and quarterly checks. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Megger, cover, silica gel. Permits: None. Parts: Desiccant.
chunks.title: MO-10 Spare motor storage and preservation

chunks.text: MO-10 Spare motor storage and preservation – Step 1 (Preparation): Store indoors, dry, off the floor, away from vibration; cover with silica gel inside the cover. Accept: Stored correctly. Step 2 (Inspection): Monthly: turn the shaft by hand several turns to move the grease. Accept: Turns freely. Step 3 (Inspection): Quarterly: megger (MO-01). Accept: ≥ 100 MΩ Ready; < 5 MΩ Not ready → MO-08. Step 4 (Close-out): Record in Spare_Readiness. Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: MO-10 steps 1–4

chunks.text: Procedure MO-11 – Motor current and voltage balance check (Motor). Equipment: M-101A/B, P-201A/B, VM-101A/B. Purpose: Find supply or winding problems early. When used: Quarterly; after electrical work. Prerequisites: Partner unit running or production informed. PPE: Safety shoes, gloves (chemical-resistant), safety glasses, hard hat. Tools: Clamp meter, multimeter. Permits: Live-work permit. Parts: None.
chunks.title: MO-11 Motor current and voltage balance check

chunks.text: MO-11 Motor current and voltage balance check – Step 1 (Inspection): With the motor running at normal load, measure the 3 line currents. Accept: Recorded. Safety: Live work – electrician only, insulated PPE. Step 2 (Inspection): Measure the 3 line voltages at the starter. Accept: Within ±10% of rated; balanced. Step 3 (Inspection): Work out the imbalance (largest difference from average ÷ average). Accept: Current imbalance ≤ 10%; voltage ≤ 2% (assumed plant rule). Step 4 (Close-out): If above limit: raise a work order (MO-05, MO-06). Accept: Saved.
chunks.title: MO-11 steps 1–4

chunks.title: MG-01 Repair-or-replace review

chunks.text: MG-01 Repair-or-replace review – Step 1 (Preparation): Open the Repair_vs_Replace result on the tablet for the asset. Accept: Rules result shown. Step 2 (Inspection): Check the facts: failures in 12 months, age, repair cost vs new, downtime cost from Batch 1. Accept: Facts confirmed. Step 3 (Inspection): Check a spare or swap-in is available while deciding. Accept: Interim plan known. Step 4 (Close-out): Record decision (Repair / Repair – watch / Replace), reason and approver. Accept: Decision saved.

chunks.title: MG-02 Emergency spare part purchase

chunks.text: 2.1 Duty, standby and daily rotation – Chapter 2 Daily operation 2.1 Duty, standby and daily rotation Each pair (transfer pumps, sump pumps, screens) runs one unit while the other waits as standby. chunks.text: 8.4 Reading vibration trends – 8.4 Reading vibration trends A single reading tells you where the machine is; the trend tells you where it is going. The daily vibration check (pen on DE and NDE bearings) is plotted by the software against the zones below. The two charts are real trends from the plant data before two failures of P-101A. good watch – move checks earlier (AR-01) alarm – corrective WO within 24 h (AR-02) stop 0 2 4 6 8 mm/s 21 Oct 2025 1 Nov 2025 12 Nov 2025 23 Nov 2025 4 Dec 2025 2.8 passed failure P-101A drive-end vibration before FE-11 (bearing failure, 5 Dec 2025) FE-11 – bearing wear: steady for weeks, then a rise over about 3 weeks with bearing temperature climbing (56 → 88 °C). The technician enters a few facts on the tablet; the software fills the rest from its records (asset, readings, work orders, parts, costs, loss estimate).
